To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the flavor and acceptance of roasted almonds are negatively impacted by storage, with the most important flavor changes being the increase in lipid oxidation and decrease in Maillard reaction products.
roasted almonds stored at 39°C for 12 months had a flavor that was similar to that of fresh roasted almonds.
lipid oxidation products were the best predictors of sensory attributes associated with rancidity, while Maillard reaction products were the best predictor of consumer liking.

the chemical and sensory changes that occur during roasting and subsequent storage of almonds, and it provides a foundation for monitoring the quality of almonds during processing and storage.

the sensory profile and consumer hedonic liking of almonds is best predicted by compounds related to lipid and Maillard reaction products.
the most important volatile compounds that are related to the development of rancidity in almonds during storage are lipid oxidation products.

the most important compounds for predicting rancid and nutty flavors are lipid oxidation products and Maillard reaction products, respectively, and these compounds are important for consumer hedonic liking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the flavor of roasted almonds is a balance between Maillard and lipid oxidation reactions, which are in turn affected by roasting conditions and storage time.
lipid oxidation products are the most important compounds for predicting rancid attributes, and Maillard reaction products are most important for predicting Clean Nutty attributes.

the flavor of roasted almonds is complex, involving multiple chemical and sensory attributes, and that the sensory and chemical changes occurring during storage are predictable and can be used to monitor the quality of stored almonds.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the flavor of almonds during accelerated storage is best predicted by the volatile profiles and sensory attributes of freshly roasted almonds, rather than the volatile profile and sensory attributes after storage.
lipid oxidation and Maillard reaction products are both important in determining flavor of roasted almonds during storage.
the sensory attributes of almonds are affected by both roasting conditions and storage conditions, but the effects are not additive.
